summary: No region-specific signal was identified for Ancash: all three sources in the inventory are national in scope and contain no Ancash-specific ordinance, enforcement action, incident or institution, so the national assessment carried by the Peru record is what applies to a visit in this department.
tangentialFactors:
The inventory offers nothing for comparison at departmental level. The items it holds — a congressional restroom restriction, a national tally of killings and rights-violation cases, and a regulatory complaint record — are unlocalised to any Peruvian department, and none of them names Ancash, Huaraz or any locality within the department.

Ancash therefore has no sourced baseline against which to be ranked alongside other departments, and no per-department violence or enforcement figure exists in the material to compare with the national counts.
localsOnly:
No resident-facing finding for Ancash is sourced: the inventory records no local police practice, regional or municipal administration, health service, civil-registry procedure or community organisation specific to the department.

Whether trans residents of Ancash encounter the national rules differently from residents of Lima is not addressed anywhere in the material.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: whether any Ancash provincial or municipal authority has issued its own anti-discrimination measure, facility rule or inclusive-signage policy is not sourced either way; the inventory contains no local-government material for the department.

Unresolved: the national statistics reproduced in the inventory are not broken down by department, so Ancash's share of recorded killings and rights-violation cases is unknown and cannot be inferred from them.

Unresolved: no source documents how the national restroom restriction is enforced in practice in Ancash, including whether venue security staff in the department check identity documents, nor whether any complaint has been filed locally.
